newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Argentine port delays seen pushing freights higher.
newsitem.headline: Argentine port delays seen pushing freights higher.

text.p: Strong Argentine grain exports and loading delays in the country's ports are expected to push trans-Pacific freight rates higher particularly for Handy-sized vessels (capacity up to 25,000 tonnes), traders said on Tuesday.
"If you have commitments to deliver for December prepare for the worst, and get ready to pay at sky-high prices," a trader in a Philippines-based U.S. commodity house said.

London's Baltic Freight Index rose on Monday with a shortage of tonnage reported in most areas. The turnover of Panamaxes in particular for trips and short periods remained healthy and Handies were quoted very firm.
But Philippine flour millers said reports of shipping delays of up to 15 days in Argentine ports had not affected their plans to buy Argentine wheat.
"We're looking at January 1997 shipments. So if we order now, the Argentina suppliers will have enough time to fix our orders," an executive at a Philippine mill said.
"Just in case we decide to buy Argentina wheat we will peg our price to include costs and freight so the shipping problems will not be on our side," the executive said.
Local flour millers said on Tuesday that Argentina had offered to supply the Philippines with 70,000 tonnes of wheat for January, 1997 requirements.
Taiwan traders, who are mulling purchasing Argentine corn but have yet to tender for the 1997 crop, said they expected to see only a marginal impact from the shipping delays.
Taiwan buyers would consider Argentine corn if its price were around US$10 a tonne lower than U.S. corn during tender, one trader said.
The rise in Pacific freight rates would make Argentine corn less attractive, he added.
